'''Conny Clara Aerts''', born 26 January 1966, is a Belgian (Flemish) professor in astrophysics. She specialises in [[asteroseismology]]. She is associated with [[KU Leuven]] and [[Radboud University Nijmegen|Radboud University]], where she leads the Chair in the Astroseismology group.<ref name="ingevoerd">{{Cite web|url=https://www.ru.nl/english/people/aerts-c/|title=Search for people or departments|last=ingevoerd|first=Geen OWMS velden|website=Radboud University|language=en|access-date=2 January 2019}}</ref><ref name="www.essc.esf.org">{{Cite web|url=http://www.essc.esf.org/membership/essc-members/conny-aerts/|title=Conny Aerts – ESF – ESSC|website=www.essc.esf.org|access-date=2 January 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190416001835/http://www.essc.esf.org/membership/essc-members/conny-aerts/|archive-date=16 April 2019|url-status=dead}}</ref> In 2012, she became the first woman to be awarded the [[Francqui Prize]] in the category of Science & Technology.<ref name="www.essc.esf.org" /><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.francquifoundation.be/rapport-test/rapport-jury-aers/|title=2012 – Rapport Jury Conny Aerts – Fondation Francqui – Stichting|website=www.francquifoundation.be|access-date=2 January 2019}}</ref>   In 2022, she became the third woman to be awarded the [[Kavli Prize]] in Astrophysics for her work in [[asteroseismology]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.kavliprize.org/laureates|title=Kavli Prize Laureates|website=Kavli Prize|access-date=1 June 2022}}</ref>

== Biography ==
Aerts was born in [[Brasschaat]], Belgium. She received her Bachelor and Master in Mathematics from the [[University of Antwerp]]. She participated in the [[International Astronomical Youth Camp]] in 1987 and 1988. She then went on to complete her PhD in 1993 at [[KU Leuven]]. After completing she spent several months doing research at the University of Delaware.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.francquifoundation.be/wp-content/uploads/Rapport-Jury-Aerts_en.pdf|title=Report of Jury Conny Aerts|website=www.francquifoundation.be|access-date=2 January 2019}}</ref> She was a postdoctoral fellow with the Fund for Scientific Research from 1993 to 2001, when she was appointed lecturer at KU Leuven.<ref name="fys.kuleuven.be">{{Cite web|url=https://fys.kuleuven.be/ster/research-projects/prosperity/Conny_Aerts/Conny_Aerts|title=CONNY AERTS|website=fys.kuleuven.be|language=en|access-date=2 January 2019}}</ref> She became first associate professor in 2004, and then full professor in 2007 at KU Leuven.<ref name="fys.kuleuven.be" />

== Research ==
In her research, she uses the star oscillations to determine the internal rotation profile of stars.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.interseismology.org/conny-aerts.html|title=Conny Aerts|website=Interseismology|access-date=2 January 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190103055848/http://www.interseismology.org/conny-aerts.html|archive-date=3 January 2019|url-status=dead}}</ref> The oscillations are obtained from both ground and space-based telescopes.<ref name="Expat Guide to Belgium | Expatica-2012">{{Cite web|url=https://www.expatica.com/be/astronomer-wins-prestigious-francqui-prize/|title=Astronomer wins prestigious Francqui Prize|date=11 May 2012|website=Expat Guide to Belgium {{!}} Expatica|language=en-US|access-date=2 January 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190103060102/https://www.expatica.com/be/astronomer-wins-prestigious-francqui-prize/|archive-date=3 January 2019|url-status=dead}}</ref> In her PROSPERITY project, she used data obtained from the [[CoRoT]] satellite and the NASA [[Kepler (spacecraft)|Kepler]] satellite.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://fys.kuleuven.be/ster/research-projects/prosperity/welcome|title=ERC ADVANCED GRANT|website=fys.kuleuven.be|language=en|access-date=2 January 2019}}</ref> She is currently the Belgian principal investigator on the [[PLATO (spacecraft)|PLATO]] mission.<ref name="PLATOMission-2018">{{Cite web|url=https://platomission.com/2018/05/03/connie-aerts/|title=Conny Aerts|last=PLATOMission|date=3 May 2018|language=en|access-date=2 January 2019}}</ref>

Aerts developed methodology using Gaussian mixture classification to analyse the data.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://fys.kuleuven.be/ster/staff/conny-aerts/conny-aerts|title=Conny Aerts|website=fys.kuleuven.be|language=en|access-date=2 January 2019}}</ref> She uses this to determine the star structure and inform stellar models within [[Stellar evolution|stellar evolution theory]]. With these techniques she has made a number of discoveries, including that of non-rigid rotation in giant stars.<ref name="www.essc.esf.org" /><ref name="fys.kuleuven.be" />

The theoretical models she develops based on the star oscillations also allow her determine the age of stars with a high accuracy.<ref name="ingevoerd" /><ref name="Expat Guide to Belgium | Expatica-2012" />

Aerts has twice been awarded an Advanced Grant by the European Research Council (ERC): in 2008 for PROSPERITY, and again in 2015 for a project entitled MAMSIE<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://fys.kuleuven.be/ster/research-projects/mamsie|title=MAMSIE project|date=3 May 2018|language=en|access-date=2 January 2019}}</ref> (Mixing and Angular Momentum Transport of Massive Stars).

== Outreach ==
Aerts is Vice-Dean of Communication & Outreach at the Faculty of Science at KU Leuven.<ref name="www.iac.es">{{Cite web|url=http://www.iac.es/divulgacion.php?op1=16&op2=402&id=122&lang=en|title=Instituto de Astrofísica de Canarias – IAC – Educational Outreach|website=www.iac.es|access-date=2 January 2019}}</ref> She is outspoken about the need to increase gender equality in the sciences,<ref name="www.iac.es" /> and is a member of the International Astronomical Union Women in Astronomy Working Group.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://astronomy.swin.edu.au/IAU-WIAWG/members/OC.html|title=IAU Working Group on Women in Astronomy|website=astronomy.swin.edu.au|access-date=2 January 2019|archive-date=10 March 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110310010729/http://astronomy.swin.edu.au/IAU-WIAWG/members/OC.html|url-status=dead}}</ref>
As of 2026, Aerts became a co-editor of the ''[[Annual Review of Astronomy and Astrophysics]]''.<ref name="ED">{{cite web |title=Annual Review of Astronomy and Astrophysics, Current Editorial Committee |url=https://www.annualreviews.org/db/directory?0000,astro |website=Annual Reviews |access-date=12 August 2026}}</ref>

== Prizes and recognition ==
* In 2010 she was elected Honorary Fellow of the Royal Astronomical Society.<ref name="www.flanderstoday.eu">{{Cite web|url=http://www.flanderstoday.eu/current-affairs/face-flanders-21|title=Face of Flanders {{!}} Flanders Today|website=www.flanderstoday.eu|access-date=2 January 2019|archive-date=3 January 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190103060105/http://www.flanderstoday.eu/current-affairs/face-flanders-21|url-status=dead}}</ref>
* In 2011 she was elected Member of the Royal Flemish Academy for Sciences and Arts.<ref name="www.flanderstoday.eu" /> 
* In 2012 she won the Francqui prize.<ref name="Expat Guide to Belgium | Expatica-2012" />
* In 2016 she received the title of Commander of the Order of Leopold.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.flanderstoday.eu/current-affairs/week-brief-25-july|title=The week in brief: 25 July {{!}} Flanders Today|website=www.flanderstoday.eu|access-date=2 January 2019|archive-date=28 July 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160728131024/http://www.flanderstoday.eu/current-affairs/week-brief-25-july|url-status=dead}}</ref>
* In 2017 she was awarded the Hintze Lecture at Oxford University, delivering also a public lecture entitled "Starquakes expose stellar heartbeats".<ref name="fys.kuleuven.be" />
* In 2018 she was awarded the ESA Lodewijk Woltjer Lecture for her work in the field of asteroseismology.<ref name="PLATOMission-2018" />
* In 2019, asteroid [[413033 Aerts]] was named in her honor.<ref name="MPC-object" /> The official {{MoMP|413033|naming citation}} was published by the [[Minor Planet Center]] on 18 May 2019 ({{small|[[Minor Planet Circulars|M.P.C.]] 114955}}).<ref name="MPC-Circulars-Archive" />
* In 2020 she was awarded the Research Foundation – Flanders (FWO) Excellence Prize in Exact Sciences.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.fwo.be/en/news/news/laureates-fwo-excellence-prizes/|title=Laureates FWO-Excellence prizes|website=FWO|access-date=1 July 2020}}</ref>
* In 2022 she was awarded the [[Kavli Prize]] in Astrophysics.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.kavliprize.org/events/kavli-prize-announcement-2022|title=Kavli Prize Announcement 2022|website=Kavli Prize|date=June 2022 |access-date=1 June 2022}}</ref>
* In 2024 she received the [[Crafoord Prize]] in Astronomy.<ref>[https://www.crafoordprize.se/news/this-years-crafoord-laureates-can-see-inside-stars-and-describe-geometric-shapes/ Crafoord Prize 2024]</ref>
